name: sgs/nav-bar-menu
title: SGS Nav Bar Menu
description: The site's primary navigation BAR — a flat horizontal row of real links on desktop; below the collapse point it becomes a burger that opens a separate sgs/nav-drawer-menu via the shared sgs/nav Interactivity store. Renders dropdowns and mega panels. Menu content comes from a native WordPress menu. Split from the former sgs/nav-menu (D1059) — the drawer's own accordion/drill-down list is now the separate sgs/nav-drawer-menu block.

indicator.reason: style.css declares .sgs-nav-bar-menu__indicator { pointer-events: none; } — the element is structurally unhoverable, the browser passes all pointer events through to whatever is underneath. It paints from the item Background row's own Hover swatch (itemBgHover / itemBgHoverGradient) under itemBgHoverTreatment === 'highlight' (Spec 41 FR-41-25), so its colour already carries that row's states rather than a parallel pair of its own.

submenu-bg.reason: The submenu panel's visibility is a binary open/closed disclosure toggled by the trigger, not by pointer position over the panel itself — once open, the pointer is always over some interactive CHILD, never a hoverable moment on the panel background itself. The hoverable surface inside the panel is the LINK background, which carries its own full three-state family (submenuLinkBg / submenuLinkBgHover / submenuLinkBgCurrent, Spec 41 FR-41-9) — that is where a hover fill belongs, and it is declared there.

submenu-border.reason: The panel's border sits on the same structurally non-hoverable surface as its background, for the same reason: once the panel is open the pointer is always over an interactive CHILD. Per-state border colour inside the panel belongs to the LINK, whose own three-state family (submenuLinkBg / submenuLinkBgHover / submenuLinkBgCurrent) is where a pointer-driven change is actually perceivable. submenuBorderColour is therefore Normal-only (Spec 41 FR-41-9).

wrapper.label: Nav wrapper
wrapper._note: The rendered <nav> (SGS_Container_Wrapper, composite-mirror rule R-31-9). Padding/margin ride the native spacing support; max-width is the flat attribute. navBg/navColour/navBgHover all write to the same bare $uid_sel wrapper selector (2026-08-28 fix — navBg previously only resolved via a hand-seeded attr-classification-overrides.json entry, not derivation; that override entry is now redundant, kept for now as a separate cleanup). The 12 ARRANGEMENT members (layer OUTER) — display/flex-direction/align-items/justify-content etc. — are honest GAPs: style.css:13-17 hardcodes `display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between` with no attribute behind any of it. Not fixed here — out of this task's scope (only STATE_WITHOUT_BASE cases are fixed).
wrapper._note_hover_nav: navColourHover declared 2026-09-05: render.php:872-873 emits sgs_hover_state_rules( "{$uid_sel}", 'color:…', ':focus-visible' ) — the block ROOT, so it belongs on the wrapper element, not a descendant.

bar.label: Item bar (flex row)
bar._note: The <ul class="sgs-nav-bar-menu__bar"> that actually arranges the item links — distinct from `wrapper`, which arranges the bar against the burger toggle-wrap. Remaining ARRANGEMENT members are honest GAPs (style.css:19-26 hardcodes `display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap` with no attribute). `css:grid-template-columns:count` is a pseudo-property destination tag (mirrors `css:color-gradient` — not a real CSS property, a manifest-level routing key) claiming `listColumns` as this element's grid COLUMN-COUNT destination for the converter's grid resolver (`db.attr_for_grid_column_count`), matching render.php:1603-1624's own target selector `.sgs-nav-bar-menu__bar` for the in-drawer vertical-list column count. [nav-bar-menu split, 2026-09-14: the listColumns grid-column-count destination was DRAWER-only (targeted the in-drawer vertical list) and is dropped from this block's manifest along with the attribute itself.]

item.label: Nav item (resting)
item._note: The nav item LINK — every stateful control on this element targets the <a>, never the <li> (Spec 41 FR-41-1). Three states are declared: base, `hover` (render.php's `$hover_targets` = `:hover, :focus-visible`) and `current` (`[aria-current="page"]`), so a visitor can distinguish WHERE THEY ARE from WHAT THEY ARE POINTING AT. The current-page state is operator-controllable through `itemColourCurrent` / `itemBgCurrent` / `itemFontWeightCurrent` (Spec 41 FR-41-1); `itemFontWeightCurrent` is the non-colour signal that satisfies WCAG 1.4.1 without relying on colour alone. `current` deliberately maps DIFFERENT attribute names from `hover`: the classifier's `extract-signatures.py::_record` is last-write-wins, so a state map byte-identical to `hover` silently overwrites the hover derivation and tags those attributes with a css_state they never render in. Every state member is EXPLICIT rather than left to the `{prefix}Suffix` convention — `css:font-weight`, `css:text-decoration` and `css:text-transform` each carry a base attribute AND a state sibling, and without an explicit entry per state both derive to the same (property, element, state=NULL) slot and collide on one routing destination. The base `css:font-weight` -> `itemFontWeight` entry is load-bearing for the same reason: a state entry with no base is the STATE_WITHOUT_BASE shape the manifest gate flags. `css:border-radius` -> `itemBorderRadius` is base-only — radius has no state on `SgsBorderControl` (Spec 41 FR-41-7).

indicator.label: Sliding indicator
indicator._note: The `.sgs-nav-bar-menu__indicator` sliding pill, view.js-animated behind the active/hovered item. It is rendered under `itemBgHoverTreatment === 'highlight'` and paints from the item Background row's OWN Hover swatch — `itemBgHover` / `itemBgHoverGradient`, claimed by the `item` element's `states.hover` (Spec 41 FR-41-25) — so this element routes no attribute of its own: one picker, one property, three ways of applying it. `clusters: ["fill"]` is retained (not `[]`) because the forward-resolution pass only visits a cluster's members when the cluster is declared; with an empty attrMap the fill members are honest GAPs, ungated and correct, since this element has no controls of its own. `supports.sgs.colourExemptions.indicator` records why it carries no hover state: style.css declares `.sgs-nav-bar-menu__indicator { pointer-events: none; }`, so the element is structurally unhoverable.

item-separator.label: Item separator (bar)
item-separator._note: FR-41-37 (2026-09-13) + follow-up (2026-09-14, directional sweep generalisation). The between-item vertical rule on the horizontal bar (nav-menu-css.php's item-separator block) -- a GENUINELY SEPARATE element from `item` (the link itself): this rule paints on the <li> (`.sgs-nav-bar-menu__item::after` when Sweep is active) or via longhand border-right-* on the <a>'s existing border box otherwise, never the item's own itemBorderColour/itemBorderWidth family (see nav-menu-css.php's own comment distinguishing the two). Longhand border-right-* declared explicitly (not the `border-color`/`border-width` shorthand `item` uses) because a shorthand here would reset whatever the item's own underline/row-separator family already wrote on the SAME selector when Sweep is off. `itemSeparatorHoverTreatment`/`itemSeparatorSweepAngle` are declared `role:behaviour` (attr-classification-overrides.json) rather than routed through this manifest -- they are control-selector/parameter attrs, not paintable CSS values, matching the established pattern for itemBorderHoverTreatment/borderHoverAnimationDirection's sibling on the `item` element above.

featured.label: Featured item
featured._note: render.php:431-459. featuredFontWeightHover is a genuine hover-state weight change (only emitted when it differs from resting), declared under `text` cluster's css:font-weight member. featuredColourGradient added 2026-09-04 (mirrors burgerColourGradient's shape) -- explicit attrMap since css:color-gradient is not resolved by the default {prefix}Suffix convention, same reason burgerColourGradient needed one. Resting LABEL form only; PILL form and the submenu-inheritance custom property stay flat (see render.php comments). featuredBgGradient/featuredBgHoverGradient added 2026-09-06 (D958, Bean-directed preset-to-gradient upgrade) -- non-empty wins over the resolved featuredBg/featuredBgHover slug+hex; when active the pill foreground skips WCAG contrast-against-background maths (no single hex to test) and uses the operator's own flat colour instead (see render.php). The submenu-inheritance custom property stays hex-only, same scope boundary as featuredColourGradient above.

burger.label: Burger toggle
burger._note: burgerColour is the icon TEXT colour (css:color, render.php:466-469); burgerHoverColour drives the button's HOVER background-color (render.php:479-482, was 470-473 pre-fix), which previously had no resting counterpart — a client could style the hover fill but never the button's own resting fill (STATE_WITHOUT_BASE, Spec 35 FR-35-5). Fixed 2026-07-21 by adding the `burgerBg` base attribute + inspector control (edit.js Burger panel, Normal state) so css:background-color now resolves at base too. Unset burgerBg renders byte-identical to before (style.css:73-88 `background:none` default). 2026-09-05: `css:color`->burgerColour (render.php:1189-1196), `css:background-color`->burgerBg (render.php:1210-1213) and `states.hover.css:color`->burgerColourHover (render.php:1199-1201, sgs_hover_state_rules on `:hover, :focus-visible`) declared EXPLICITLY. Two DB-consistency findings drove this: (a) burgerColour + burgerColourHover both derived to (color, burger, state=NULL), colliding on one routing slot -- the hover entry is what separates them; (b) burgerBg carried a rogue `css_property='background-color'` seed present in NEITHER the derived classifier layer NOR the overrides, so it would have vanished on the next reseed. The manifest is the durable source; the stray seed is not removed here because the attribute genuinely paints that property.

sublink.label: Submenu link
sublink._note: The submenu LINK — <a class="sgs-nav-bar-menu__sublink">, painted at render.php's own scoped `.sgs-nav-bar-menu__sublink{...}` rule. It carries three states: base, `hover` (`sgs_hover_state_rules()` on `:hover, :focus-visible`) and `current` (`[aria-current="page"]`), matching the bar item's own three-state model (Spec 41 FR-41-1 / FR-41-9). `"prefix": ""` is a deliberate, permanent opt-out from the `{prefix}Suffix` convention: a `submenu` prefix would wrongly claim submenuAlign/Caret/CloseGrace/MinWidth/Padding and the whole submenuBorder* family, which belong to the submenu PANEL (the `submenu-panel` element) rather than to this anchor. The `submenu`-prefixed typography attributes that DO belong to this anchor reach it through the explicit attrMap entries above, one per property — that is the resolution, not a prefix (Spec 41 FR-41-22c). With an empty prefix nothing here resolves by convention, so every member is explicit by necessity: each state's `css:color`, `css:background-color`, `css:font-weight`, `css:text-decoration` and `css:text-transform` names a DIFFERENT attribute from its base sibling, because without an explicit entry a base and its state sibling both derive to (property, sublink, state=NULL) and collide on one routing slot. `"fill"` is declared alongside `"text"` so the forward-resolution pass actually visits css:background-color / css:background-image and consults this attrMap; a cluster that is not declared is never iterated. submenuColourGradient is routed as a DIRECT declaration (sgs_text_colour_decl / sgs_resolve_text_colour_or_gradient) rather than a colour-valued custom property, because a `var(--x, …)` chain feeding a fixed `color:` declaration cannot switch to `background-image` for a gradient (survey.js's `paints-via-colour-valued-custom-property` refusal reason). [nav-bar-menu split, 2026-09-14: the sublinkMarker* fill/fill-gradient entries were DRAWER-only per the classification report (the marker's own CSS is scoped `.sgs-nav-drawer …`, so it never painted anything in the bar dropdown) — dropped along with the attributes.]

submenu-panel.label: Submenu panel
submenu-panel._note: The floating dropdown PANEL — <div class="sgs-nav-bar-menu__submenu"> — as distinct from the links inside it, which are the `sublink` element (Spec 41 FR-41-9). Base only: NO `states` key at all, because the panel has neither a hover nor a current state for any property. Its visibility is a binary open/closed disclosure toggled by the trigger; once open the pointer is always over an interactive CHILD, so a pointer-driven change on the panel surface itself is never perceivable — the hoverable surface inside the panel is the LINK background (submenuLinkBg / submenuLinkBgHover / submenuLinkBgCurrent on `sublink`). Recorded as `supports.sgs.colourExemptions.submenu-bg` and `.submenu-border`. `"prefix": ""` for the same reason `sublink` carries it: a `submenu` prefix would claim submenuColour* and the submenu typography family, which belong to the LINK. Every member is therefore explicit.

sgs._note_sweep_eligibility: The ONE declarative source for the Sweep-treatment eligibility predicate, read by BOTH surfaces — edit.js decides whether to offer the Sweep segment, render.php decides whether to emit Sweep CSS — with neither re-deriving the rule (Spec 41 FR-41-26). It is NOT an `elements` entry and routes no CSS property; it sits beside colourExemptions / hideExtensions / boxFamilies. Three keys per row: `blockingBackgroundAttrs` (Sweep is withdrawn when ANY named attribute is non-empty, because background-clip:text clips the element's whole background-painting area to the glyph shapes — every state's background counts, not just the resting one), `blockingGradientAttrs` (the row's own text gradient writes background-image on the identical selector, so whichever loses is invisible) and `glyphGuard` (background-clip:text needs glyphs to grip; null means the element always has them). Every attribute named below must exist in `attributes` — a typo reads as permanently empty, so the predicate would always pass and the rule would silently cease to exist.

attributes._note_nav_fill: Nav CONTAINER surface (2026-07-28). The block previously had NO fill controls at all — only per-ITEM colours — so a client could never sit the bar on its own surface. Scope is deliberately SURFACE ONLY: border/radius/divider were built and then REMOVED the same day (Bean ruling) because the pill-nav and bordered-nav patterns that justify them are whole-HEADER treatments, and sgs/site-header already declares `color` + `__experimentalBorder` supports for exactly that. Do not re-add them here without a header-level reason. Defaults unset, so an untouched nav renders byte-identically. Because the drawer holds its OWN sgs/nav-menu instance, these also give fully independent drawer styling with no extra plumbing.

navColourGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the nav text with a background-clip:text mechanism instead of a flat colour (D956 text-colour gradient rollout). Non-empty wins over navColour. Safe unconditionally -- navBg already paints on a separate ::after layer (sgs_block_background_layer_css()), never this same selector.

itemColourGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the resting nav-item text with a background-clip:text mechanism instead of a flat colour (D956 text-colour gradient rollout). Non-empty wins over itemColour. Safe unconditionally -- itemBg already paints on a ::before layer (D942 recipe item 1), never this same selector. See itemColourHoverGradient for the Hover-state sibling.

itemBgGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the resting nav-item background via the same ::before layer as itemBg (D942 recipe item 1); non-empty wins over the flat itemBg colour, mirroring itemColourGradient's sibling-wins pattern.

itemColourHoverGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the Hover-state nav-item text, mirroring itemColourGradient's background-clip:text mechanism. Non-empty wins over itemColourHover. Offered in the editor ONLY while itemSmartContrast is OFF (the default) -- when itemSmartContrast is ON, itemColourHover auto-computes a safe solid colour for WCAG contrast against itemBgHover, which a gradient cannot meaningfully replace, so a stored value here is ignored by render.php while the swap is active rather than silently reappearing.

featuredColourGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the featured bar item's LABEL-form text with a background-clip:text mechanism instead of a flat colour (mirrors burgerColourGradient). Non-empty wins over featuredColour. Resting LABEL form only (no featuredBg set) -- the PILL form (featuredBg set) keeps its WCAG-contrast-resolved flat foreground, and the submenu inheritance custom property (--sgs-nm-featured-colour) stays flat-only because its consumer paints a background on the same selector (see render.php).

featuredBgGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the featured item's PILL-form background (background-image custom-property-gradient pattern, D958 upgrade from slug-only). Non-empty wins over the resolved featuredBg slug/hex. When active, the pill's foreground SKIPS the WCAG contrast-against-background computation (sgs_wcag_preferred_text_colour_for_bg() needs ONE background hex; a gradient has none) and uses the operator's own FLAT featuredColour/featuredColourHover choice instead -- never the gradient-capable text resolve, which would collide with this same background-image on the same selector (see render.php comment at the featured-item paint block, and featuredColourGradient's note above for the identical precedent on the flat-hex pill form). The submenu-inherited featured item (--sgs-nm-featured-bg custom property) is NOT extended to carry this gradient -- same documented scope boundary as featuredColourGradient's submenu gap above.

featuredBgHoverGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the featured item's PILL-form :hover/:focus-visible background (mirrors featuredBgGradient, D958). Non-empty wins over the resolved featuredBgHover slug/hex. Same WCAG-skip rationale as featuredBgGradient: the hover foreground uses the operator's own flat featuredColourHover (falling back to featuredColour) rather than computing WCAG contrast against a gradient.

burgerFontSize.description: Spec 41 Wave 2 J1. Unset renders font-size:inherit (helpers-typography.php's sgs_typography_css_rule(), $inherit_font_size_when_blank) — inherits the theme's real body font-size rather than the UA <button> default (~13.3px).

burgerFontFamily.description: Spec 41 Wave 2 J1. Unset renders font-family:inherit ($inherit_font_family_when_blank) — inherits the theme's real body font rather than the UA default (Arial).

burgerLetterSpacing.description: Tier object mirroring submenuLetterSpacing's shape. Default resolves to 0.05em (see burgerLetterSpacingUnit).

attributes._note_three_state_model: Spec 41: every stateful control on this block targets the LINK, in three states — Normal, Hover (:hover, :focus-visible) and Current ([aria-current="page"]). The nav BAR keeps two states (navBg/navColour + their Hover siblings): a bar is never 'the current page'. The submenu PANEL keeps one (FR-41-9): its visibility is a binary open/closed disclosure, so the hoverable surface inside it is the LINK, which carries the full three-state family. Every new small string attribute below is declared WITHOUT a JSON enum and is validated in PHP instead: an out-of-enum stored value is silently coerced back to the block.json default with no error, which bites hardest via a programmatic writer (the cloning converter, a theme pattern) setting the attribute directly. The one exception is the pre-existing itemTextDecoration, which carries a real enum and keeps it — a disclosed asymmetry with its own hover sibling, not an oversight.

itemBgCurrentGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the current-page nav item's background via the same ::before layer as itemBg; non-empty wins over the flat itemBgCurrent colour.

itemBgHoverGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the hovered nav item's background via the same ::before layer as itemBg; non-empty wins over the flat itemBgHover colour. It completes the row's three-state gradient set (itemBgGradient / this / itemBgCurrentGradient) and is what the Highlight treatment paints with when the operator picks a gradient (Spec 41 FR-41-25).

itemFontWeightCurrent.description: The non-colour current-page signal (Spec 41 FR-41-6), so the state is distinguishable without relying on colour alone. String, not number — matches itemFontWeight.

itemFontWeightHover.description: String, not number — matches itemFontWeight and itemFontWeightCurrent. A weight change on hover can reflow the bar; the control's help text carries that caution.

itemSmartContrast.description: Opt-in AUTO-FIX: when ON, resolves the item's foreground automatically so it stays readable against whatever background the item is sitting on (Spec 41 FR-41-5). Default OFF (changed 2026-09-13, Bean-directed): an operator's explicit itemColourHover is now respected as-authored by default — no silent swap. The readability CHECK itself is unconditional and always warns in the editor inspector regardless of this setting; only the automatic colour SWAP is gated on it.

itemBorderWidth.description: REVERSED 2026-09-15 (Bean, live on the real homepage: read as an unwanted shadow/border on every item at rest). Default is now OFF (empty object, no border painted) until the operator sets a width. FR-41-36’s original locked default was bottom-only, 1px, always visible. On the horizontal bar this is the ITEM UNDERLINE â€” a bottom-edge text-indicator under one item's own label. On a vertical list (this same instance rendered inside a nav-drawer, or a submenu-root stacked in-drawer) the identical bottom edge is geometrically a ROW SEPARATOR between two adjacent rows. One shared attribute family paints both, by design (2026-09-13 terminology pass) â€” see nav-menu-css.php's item-border comment for the full reasoning. Not to be confused with itemSeparatorWidth, the independent NEW vertical divider between top-level bar items (FR-41-37).

itemBorderRadius.description: A FLAT corner object of CSS length STRINGS, read by sgs_corner_object_shorthand(), which looks for exactly topLeft / topRight / bottomRight / bottomLeft. NOT the {"desktop":{}} tier envelope — that shape belongs to BLOCK-ROOT radii read by sgs_border_radius_tiers(); used here it would carry no corner keys, the helper would return null, and the radius would silently vanish. Per-element precedent: sgs/product-card::ctaBorderRadius.

itemBorderColour.description: FR-41-36 locked default: underline/row-separator colour at rest (bar: item underline; drawer: row separator — see itemBorderWidth's note).

itemBorderColourHover.description: FR-41-36 locked default: underline/row-separator colour on hover.

itemBorderColourCurrent.description: FR-41-36 locked default: underline/row-separator colour on current/active — same colour as Hover; the absence of a bg fill is what distinguishes Current from Hover.

itemColourHoverTreatment.description: How the item TEXT colour changes on hover: none / swap / sweep. The Sweep option is offered and emitted only when supports.sgs.sweepEligibility.itemColourHoverTreatment passes (Spec 41 FR-41-26). PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

itemBgHoverTreatment.description: How the item BACKGROUND changes on hover: none / swap / highlight. 'highlight' renders the sliding pill, painting from itemBgHover / itemBgHoverGradient (Spec 41 FR-41-25). PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

itemBorderHoverTreatment.description: How the item BORDER colour changes on hover: none / swap / sweep. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

sweepAngle.description: Directional sweep angle (FR-41-37 follow-up, 2026-09-13) -- standard CSS gradient-angle degrees (0=to top, 90=to right, 180=to bottom, 270=to left), the same convention @wordpress/components's AnglePickerControl uses. Governs the item border/underline Sweep (itemBorderHoverTreatment==='sweep'). Default 90 reproduces the retired borderHoverAnimationDirection=left-to-right output pixel-for-pixel; 270 reproduces right-to-left. See includes/sweep-css.php.

itemSeparatorWidth.description: FR-41-37 (2026-09-13) — the NEW, independent vertical divider between adjacent TOP-LEVEL bar items (a right-edge rule), separate from itemBorderWidth (the item's own underline/row-separator). Genuinely distinct from FR-41-7's existing 'set itemBorderWidth.right for a vertical divider' option: that option shares itemBorderColour/Hover/Current with the bottom-edge underline (one colour family, two edges), so it cannot be styled independently — this attribute family can. Bar-only by construction (not rendered in-drawer, where a vertical list has no 'adjacent item' in that axis). No Current state — a between-item rule is not itself a page. Hover treatment (plain colour swap, or a directional sweep) is controlled by itemSeparatorHoverTreatment/itemSeparatorSweepAngle below, shipped as a follow-up the same day (see includes/sweep-css.php).

itemSeparatorStyle.description: FR-41-37. solid / dashed / dotted / none. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

itemSeparatorColour.description: FR-41-37 — Normal-state colour, matching the same subtle default (border-light, not accent) the underline/row-separator family uses at rest, for one consistent visual language across all 4 separator contexts.

itemSeparatorColourHover.description: FR-41-37 — Hover-state colour, matching the underline/row-separator family's own Hover token.

itemSeparatorHoverTreatment.description: FR-41-37 follow-up (2026-09-13). How the item separator changes on hover: none / swap / sweep. Sweep is offered and emitted only when supports.sgs.sweepEligibility.itemSeparatorHoverTreatment passes. Default 'swap' preserves the original shipped behaviour (a plain border-right-color change) byte-for-byte. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

itemSeparatorSweepAngle.description: FR-41-37 follow-up (2026-09-13). Directional sweep angle for the item separator (same convention as sweepAngle -- CSS gradient-angle degrees). Default 180 (to bottom) is a sensible vertical default for a right-edge divider; shown only when itemSeparatorHoverTreatment is 'sweep'. See includes/sweep-css.php.

submenuColourCurrent.description: Current-page ('you are here') submenu row text colour. Defaults to the `text` (dark brown) token (2026-09-14 root-cause fix, QC council finding): the prior empty default fell through to a hardcoded `primary-dark` fallback measuring only 2.35:1 against the current-row background — well under WCAG AA's 4.5:1 floor. `text` against `submenuLinkBgCurrent`'s `surface-alt` default measures 14.31:1 on the framework's default palette and 12.55:1 on Mama's Munches (both WCAG AA, verified via wcag-contrast.js maths). Chosen as a fixed default token, not a runtime contrast computation, per Bean's ruling that defaults should not depend on a contrast-check mechanism.

submenuLinkBg.description: Normal-state submenu row background. Defaults to the palette's cream `surface` token (2026-09-14 root-cause fix, QC council finding: the drawer's nested submenu had no reliable opaque background of its own, so its row text was checked for contrast against the DRAWER's own arbitrary `drawerBg` instead of a real paint surface). Giving the row an explicit, deterministic background means the drawer no longer needs a runtime drawerBg-aware contrast computation to stay legible — the row always paints its own cream surface regardless of what colour the surrounding drawer uses. `text` (dark brown) on `surface` measures 11.86:1 (WCAG AA). Shared by both the bar's dropdown panel and the drawer's nested/accordion submenu (one attribute family, FR-41-36) — verified not to visually regress the bar dropdown, whose panel already defaults to a near-identical surface-alt/surface token chain.

submenuLinkBgHover.description: Hover-state submenu row background. Defaults to the brand's `primary` pink fill (2026-09-14 root-cause fix, QC council finding: the prior `accent-light` default paired with the also-default `accent` hover TEXT colour produced a same-hue-family combination measuring only 1.35:1 — near-invisible hover text, worst on the drawer where the row had no opaque background of its own to separate the two accents visually). `submenuColourHover` now default-closes to `text` (dark brown) at the PHP layer (nav-menu-submenu-css.php), which measures 5.28:1 against this `primary` fill (WCAG AA) — a clear, on-brand hover signal distinct from both the cream Normal state and the pink-tint Current state.

submenuLinkBgCurrent.description: Current-page ('you are here') submenu row background. Defaults to `surface-alt` (2026-09-14 correction — was `surface-pink`, a token that exists ONLY in the Mama's Munches per-client theme-snapshot.json, not in the framework's own theme.json; on any other site it resolved to an undefined CSS variable with no fallback, painting nothing. `surface-alt` is a real framework token every theme.json defines — a subtly raised/alt surface, the same convention a 'currently selected row' uses in an ordinary list). Visually distinct from both the cream Normal row (`surface`) and the solid `primary` Hover fill, while staying closer in tone to Normal than Hover — the standard 'you are here, but not being pointed at' affordance. Paired with `submenuColourCurrent`'s `text` default: 14.31:1 on the framework's default palette, 12.55:1 on Mama's Munches (both WCAG AA, verified via wcag-contrast.js maths).

submenuLinkBgGradient.description: Normal-state gradient sibling of submenuLinkBg; non-empty wins over the flat colour.

submenuLinkBorderWidth.description: FR-41-36 (C1) — the submenu ROW's own row-separator border (a horizontal line between two adjacent rows, both in the bar's dropdown panel AND a drawer's nested/accordion-expanded submenu — same mechanism, same selector), distinct from submenuBorderWidth (the PANEL's outer border). Defaults to a bottom-only 1px so an untouched dropdown/drawer-nested row shows the universal always-visible separator (2026-09-13 terminology pass — was called "item-divider").

submenuLinkBorderColour.description: FR-41-36 (C1) — Normal-state row-separator colour token, locked by Spec 41 §FR-41-36's colour table.

submenuLinkBorderColourHover.description: FR-41-36 (C1) — Hover/Current-state row-separator colour token, locked by Spec 41 §FR-41-36's colour table. No separate Current colour: the spec's table gives this row only Normal/Hover language for the separator.

submenuColourHoverTreatment.description: How the submenu LINK text colour changes on hover: none / swap / sweep. Sweep is offered and emitted only when supports.sgs.sweepEligibility.submenuColourHoverTreatment passes. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

submenuLinkBgHoverTreatment.description: How the submenu LINK background changes on hover: none / swap. Two options only — there is no Highlight on this row. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

submenuAnimation.description: The submenu panel's open animation: none / fade / slide-down. PHP-validated, no JSON enum. FR-41-1 (F1) locked default: fade — a pure-opacity transition with no directional assumption, safe regardless of overflow-flip repositioning, and degrades cleanly under prefers-reduced-motion.

submenuBorderRadius.description: The submenu panel's corner radius — the same FLAT corner object shape as itemBorderRadius (topLeft / topRight / bottomRight / bottomLeft, CSS length strings, read by sgs_corner_object_shorthand()). Its default stays EMPTY: the panel already renders its own radius from --sgs-nm-submenu-radius with a token fallback, so there is no behaviour here for a default to preserve.

submenuBorderColourGradient.description: Normal-state gradient sibling of submenuBorderColour; non-empty wins over the flat colour.

submenuShadowColour.description: The shadow's colour. The name is fixed by ShadowControl.js::shadowAttrKeys, which composes it as <base>Colour.

submenuFontSize.description: A {desktop,tablet,mobile} TIER OBJECT, mirroring itemFontSize. There are deliberately no submenuFontSizeTablet / submenuFontSizeMobile siblings: TypographyControls and sgs_typography_css_rule() both branch on whether the stored value is an object and keep all three tiers inside this one attribute, so flat tier keys would have zero writers and zero readers.

triggerMode.description: What the menu button shows: icon / text / icon-and-text. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

triggerMagnetRadius.description: Pull radius in pixels, 20-400 — the range matches fx-magnet.js's own clamp.

triggerMagnetStrength.description: Pull strength, 2-80 — the range matches fx-magnet.js's own clamp.

burgerColourHoverTreatment.description: How the menu button's ICON/TEXT colour changes on hover: none / swap / sweep. Sweep is offered and emitted only when supports.sgs.sweepEligibility.burgerColourHoverTreatment passes. Governs burgerColour / burgerColourHover (the icon colour), NOT burgerHoverColour (the button's hover BACKGROUND) — the two names are anagram-close and govern different properties. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

burgerBgHoverTreatment.description: How the menu button's BACKGROUND changes on hover: none / swap. Two options only. Governs burgerBg / burgerHoverColour. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.
